items.title: 54270_Doc Cheatham oral history interview
items.q: he left me there and Virgil Williams and -- put the band in my charge, you know.

ctx.x: Yes, Dreamland was really jumping at that time. But he got out of it and a fellow named Virgil

Williams took it over. So when Albert Wynn -- left the Dreamland, he left me there and Virgil Williams and -- put the band in my charge, you know. So naturally I was young, with that job, I didn't know what it was all about, so he wasn't paying, he was getting a band every night and wasn't paying the musicians. He would give me a book at the end of the night -- a ledger and he would give me maybe $20.00. And I'd sign my name at the bottom of this ledger. And I'd give the musicians -- you'd divide it up, whatever…

The union didn't believe it because they knew this guy was a crook. There was only one guy believed that I ran away with some money and that was my best friend, from Nashville, the drummer, by name of Hosea Jose Duff. Now he -- I brought him to Chicago to play with me in the Dreamland and he, right to this day, believes that I ran away with the band's money.
